name: Install and exchange meters
summary: Meter technicians replace smart meters whose Measurement Canada seal period is ending or whose lot failed sampling, replace failed and non-communicating meters, and install meters for new services and generators. Each job is planned onto a daily route, the technician drives to the site, checks hazards and the customer-owned meter base, swaps the meter, confirms it joins the AMI network and records the old and new meter readings, which must reach the billing system and the provincial repository before the next bill. Delays come from waiting for technician capacity, notice periods for campaigns, blocked access, damaged meter bases, winter weather and transformer-rated meters that need two technicians and an outage.

baseline.org_archetype: A municipally owned Ontario distributor of about 350,000 meters with an in-house metering team, a meter shop and mobile work orders on tablets.
baseline.notes: One case is one meter installation or exchange, from order creation to the meter change being accepted by the provincial repository.

trigger: A meter order is created by meter data analysts, a seal-expiry or sampling-failure campaign, a new service or a generation connection.
end_state: The new meter is installed, communicating and recorded in the CIS and MDM/R, or the order is deferred until the customer repairs the meter base.

volume.seasonality: Campaign exchanges run mostly April to November; winter months carry trouble exchanges and new services. New services peak in late summer and fall with housing completions.

evidence.note: Organisation file volume kept. About 420 new services a month (organisation file driver) plus failed and non-communicating meters, with the rest from seal-expiry and sampling campaigns; smart meters installed around 2006-2010 with 10-year initial and 8-year subsequent periods for qualifying electronic meters (e26) reached expiry in 2016-2022.

surge.cause: Measurement Canada sampling failure or seal expiry of a large meter lot, forcing a replacement campaign

evidence.note: Lots that reach the end of their reverification period without a sampling extension must be removed from service (e26); size and frequency are the author's estimate.
Org file has 12 meter technicians covering field work and the meter shop; about 10 FTE on installs and exchanges. Loaded cost from the organisation file (wage x 1.40).
Meter orders are planned and routed in the mobile workforce system by a planner; the organisation file's process map lists only metering roles. Loaded cost from the organisation file (wage x 1.40).
Commercial outage coordination, weather calls and field audits. Loaded cost from the organisation file (wage x 1.40).
Resolves rejected change records. Loaded cost from the organisation file (wage x 1.40).

systems.name: Mobile workforce management and field tablets
Geographic information system (asset and network model)
ERP: general ledger, work orders, purchasing, inventory, fixed assets
Provincial Meter Data Management/Repository (IESO Smart Metering Entity) portal

resources.name: Light vehicle (pickup or van) for locators, meter technicians, inspectors and field service

steps.name: Receive and check meter order
steps.description: A work planner opens the new meter order in the CIS (from metering analysts, a seal-expiry campaign list, a new service or a generation connection), checks the meter form, voltage and class against the premise record and whether instrument transformers are involved, and fixes missing details.

error.defect_description: Wrong meter form or class on the order.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of residential and commercial meter exchange work at an Ontario distributor in 2019-2022. Campaign orders are bulk-loaded, so per-order time is small.

steps.name: Classify order and plan route
steps.description: The planner groups the order by type and area: seal-expiry campaign exchanges are batched by street, trouble exchanges by district, new services wait for their connection date, and transformer-rated commercial meters go to the metering supervisor to arrange an outage.

evidence.note: Seal (reverification) periods of 6 to 10 years initial and 4 to 8 years subsequent for electronic meters drive campaign exchanges (e26); mix of order types is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Notify customers of campaign exchange
steps.description: The CIS produces notification letters, emails or automated calls for every premise in the campaign route, telling the customer that the meter will be replaced, that a brief interruption is possible and that an adult may need to give access.

evidence.note: Hydro One notifies customers by email, text, call or letter several weeks ahead and requires an adult to give access when needed (h1meter); notice period is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for ESA authorization and connection date
steps.description: New service and generation meters wait until the customer's electrician passes the Electrical Safety Authority inspection and the line or cable crew sets the connection date, so the meter is installed when the service is energized.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 22/04 and the Ontario Electrical Safety Code: ESA authorization before a new service is connected

evidence.note: Author's estimate of residential and commercial meter exchange work at an Ontario distributor in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Arrange outage for transformer-rated meter
steps.description: The metering supervisor contacts the business customer and the customer's electrician to agree a time when the main can be opened or a bypass used, books two technicians and, where the utility must isolate, a line crew window.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of residential and commercial meter exchange work at an Ontario distributor in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Assign order to a technician route
steps.description: The planner places the order on a meter technician's daily route in the mobile workforce system, balancing campaign volume against urgent trouble exchanges and the technicians available that day.

next.condition: extreme cold, ice or deep snow

evidence.note: Author's estimate of residential and commercial meter exchange work at an Ontario distributor in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Postpone route for weather
steps.description: The metering supervisor postpones outdoor exchange routes in extreme cold, freezing rain or deep snow that blocks meter access, and the orders return to the next available day.

control.basis: Utility cold-weather and slip hazard work rules

evidence.note: Author's estimate of residential and commercial meter exchange work at an Ontario distributor in 2019-2022. Ottawa winters.

steps.name: Pick tested meters and seals
steps.description: At the start of the day the technician collects programmed, tested meters, seals and blanks from the meter shop, scans each serial number to the route and loads the light vehicle.

error.defect_description: Wrong meter type loaded for the premise.

next.condition: next stop is a nearby campaign premise

evidence.note: Author's estimate of residential and commercial meter exchange work at an Ontario distributor in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Drive to next campaign premise
steps.description: On a campaign route the next premise is usually on the same street or a few blocks away, so the technician moves the vehicle a short distance.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of residential and commercial meter exchange work at an Ontario distributor in 2019-2022. Campaign production of about 20 meters a day.

steps.name: Drive to scattered site
steps.description: For trouble exchanges and new services the technician drives across the 1,116 square kilometre territory between jobs, which can take most of an hour to rural addresses.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of residential and commercial meter exchange work at an Ontario distributor in 2019-2022. Service area from the organisation file.

steps.name: Assess site hazards
steps.description: Before touching the meter the technician walks the site and records a short hazard assessment on the tablet: dogs, ice, overhead wires, a hot or damaged socket, and whether arc-rated clothing and gloves are needed for the meter class.

control.basis: Occupational Health and Safety Act and utility electrical safety rules: site hazard assessment and PPE for work on energized meter sockets

evidence.note: Author's estimate of residential and commercial meter exchange work at an Ontario distributor in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Gain access to the meter
steps.description: The technician knocks, explains the exchange, and reaches the meter. Indoor meters, locked gates, dogs, fences and stored items often block access, especially in older houses.

evidence.note: An adult must be present to give access where needed (h1meter); no-access share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Leave card and reschedule
steps.description: The technician leaves a door card asking the customer to book a time, notes the reason on the tablet, and the order goes back to the planner for another day.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of residential and commercial meter exchange work at an Ontario distributor in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Inspect meter base and service
steps.description: The technician checks the customer-owned meter base for burn marks, loose jaws, corrosion and damage, looks for signs of tampering or bypass, and confirms the meter form matches the order.

evidence.note: Meter bases are customer-owned and repairs are the customer's responsibility (h1meter); shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Issue defect notice to customer
steps.description: The technician photographs the damaged base, leaves a defect notice telling the customer to have an electrician repair it under an ESA permit, makes the site safe and closes the order as deferred.

control.basis: Utility conditions of service: the customer repairs a damaged meter base before the meter is reinstalled

evidence.note: Damaged customer-owned meter bases need repair and a repair notice is left (h1meter).

steps.name: Photograph and report suspected diversion
steps.description: The technician photographs the seal, wiring and meter, keeps the removed meter as evidence, and sends a field investigation request so field services and billing can assess unbilled consumption.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of residential and commercial meter exchange work at an Ontario distributor in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Exchange self-contained meter
steps.description: The technician reads and photographs the old meter, cuts the seal, pulls the meter from the socket, installs the new one, checks the display and rotation, and fits a new seal. Customers may lose power for a minute or two.

error.defect_description: Final read on the old meter recorded wrong.

evidence.note: Brief interruption during a standard exchange (h1meter); time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Install transformer-rated meter with two technicians
steps.description: Two technicians drive to the commercial site, isolate the service with the customer's electrician, check the current and voltage transformer ratios and wiring, install and program the meter and test socket, re-energize and confirm the readings and phase angles.

error.defect_description: Wrong multiplier or a reversed CT phase recorded.

control.basis: Occupational Health and Safety Act and utility electrical safety rules: isolation and verification before work on instrument transformer circuits

evidence.note: Author's estimate of residential and commercial meter exchange work at an Ontario distributor in 2019-2022. Transformer-rated work needs two technicians and an outage or bypass, as the organisation file states.

steps.name: Confirm meter joins AMI network
steps.description: The technician waits for the new meter to register on the mesh network, checking the tablet or calling a meter data analyst, so that the first reads will reach the repository.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of residential and commercial meter exchange work at an Ontario distributor in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Troubleshoot meter communication
steps.description: The technician checks the meter's radio, tries a replacement meter, or logs the premise as a weak-signal location for the OT team to add a range extender.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of residential and commercial meter exchange work at an Ontario distributor in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Record exchange on tablet
steps.description: The technician enters the old meter number and final read, the new meter number and initial read, seal details, time and photos in the mobile workforce form and completes the order.

error.defect_description: Meter number or read keyed wrong.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of residential and commercial meter exchange work at an Ontario distributor in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Return removed meters to the shop
steps.description: At the end of the day the technician unloads removed meters at the meter shop and scans them in for testing, sampling evidence or disposal, as Measurement Canada lot records require.

control.basis: Electricity and Gas Inspection Act: meter lot and reverification records

evidence.note: Reverification periods and extensions are tracked by meter lot (e26).

steps.name: Validate meter change record in CIS
steps.description: When the tablet syncs, the CIS checks the change record: meter number exists in inventory, reads are plausible against the last repository read, dates and multiplier match.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of residential and commercial meter exchange work at an Ontario distributor in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Resolve rejected change record
steps.description: A meter data analyst compares the rejected record with the tablet photos and the repository reads, corrects the meter number or read, or calls the technician, then resubmits.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of residential and commercial meter exchange work at an Ontario distributor in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Send meter change to repository
steps.description: The CIS sends the meter change to the provincial MDM/R so reads from the new meter are accepted and the old meter's final read closes its register.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of residential and commercial meter exchange work at an Ontario distributor in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Audit completed installation
steps.description: The metering supervisor visits a sample of completed exchanges to check the seal, installation quality, photos and that the hazard assessment was done, and coaches the technician on any finding.

control.basis: Metering quality and safety audit program

evidence.note: Author's estimate of residential and commercial meter exchange work at an Ontario distributor in 2019-2022.

exceptions.name: No access
exceptions.description: The meter cannot be reached (indoor meter, locked gate, dog); a door card is left and the order is rebooked.

exceptions.name: Damaged meter base
exceptions.description: The customer-owned base is burnt or damaged; the exchange is deferred until the customer's electrician repairs it under an ESA permit.

exceptions.name: Transformer-rated commercial meter
exceptions.description: Needs an outage window agreed with the business, two technicians and ratio and wiring checks.

exceptions.name: Rejected change record
exceptions.description: The CIS rejects the record (meter number or read keyed wrong) and an analyst corrects it from the photos.

exceptions.name: Weather postponement
exceptions.description: Extreme cold, freezing rain or deep snow postpones outdoor routes.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from meter order to meter change accepted in the repository
benchmarks.population: Ontario distributor meter exchanges and installs, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author's estimate: campaign notice of one to four weeks, route capacity of one to ten days, trouble exchanges within one to two weeks, commercial outages booked up to a month ahead.
Subsequent periods are 8 years (qualifying) and 4 years (other).

pain_points.description: Technician capacity is shared between campaign exchanges, trouble exchanges, new services and meter shop testing, so non-communicating meters can wait one to two weeks and stay estimated meanwhile.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of residential and commercial meter exchange work at an Ontario distributor in 2019-2022.

pain_points.description: About one visit in ten finds no access, and each rebooking adds a drive and a door card.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of residential and commercial meter exchange work at an Ontario distributor in 2019-2022.

pain_points.description: Meter numbers and reads keyed on the tablet are sometimes wrong, which rejects the change record or puts a spike on the customer's next bill.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of residential and commercial meter exchange work at an Ontario distributor in 2019-2022.

pain_points.description: A sampling failure turns a meter lot into a replacement campaign with a fixed deadline, which pulls technicians off other work.

evidence.note: Lots must be reverified or removed from service by the end of their reverification period.

sources.title: Bulletin E-26 (rev. 5): Reverification periods for electricity meters and metering installations
sources.supports: Initial and subsequent reverification periods for electronic meters (10/8 years qualifying, 6/4 years other); extension of a lot's period after sampling; reverification or removal from service at the end of the period.

sources.title: Electricity meter replacement
sources.supports: Customer notification by email, text, call or letter weeks ahead; an adult must give access when needed; brief interruption during a standard exchange; customer-owned meter base repairs and repair notices. Page describes Hydro One's current program and is used for practice, not volumes.

assumptions: Order type is drawn once at the classification step and again at the travel step (nearby campaign stop or scattered stop), so the simulation does not keep the two perfectly aligned; the mix is about right overall.

Hands-on time implies about 21 FTE at 2,000 jobs a month (two-technician commercial jobs add about a fifth), against 11.8 FTE stated; the organisation file has 12 meter technicians, who also staff the meter shop. Either campaign exchanges were partly contracted out (as Hydro One does with a contractor) or the technician count is low; the stated FTE assumes some contractor help.
The light vehicle is held for the drive plus the time on site; occupied minutes are attached to the travel steps.
The cs-meter-shop trigger stands for campaign lists created after sampling results or seal expiry; the 2% from generation connections is part of the 15% new-service share in the classification step.
Times and shares are the author's estimates for residential self-contained and commercial transformer-rated meters in an Ontario urban and rural territory.
